messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: rstan: initial value specification
parts:
Two questions.

1. If I provide a function that returns a list of lists, do the inner
lists need to have entries for the transformed parameters (that is,
items defined in the transformed parameters block)? I would have
thought not, but I notice that get_inits() returns inner lists that do
have those parameters.

2. Suppose my init function calls random number generators. If I
provide a seed argument to the stan call is that sufficient to assure
I'll get the same inits if I rerun with the same seed?

I'm also a bit confused by the remark that the init function can take an
optional chain_id argument. Should such a function return just the
inner list, or does it need to return a list of lists (with the outer
list having only one element?). If I use such a function does it change
the answers for 1 or 2?

Thanks.
Ross Boylan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: initial value specification
parts:
On 11/7/13, 1:02 AM, Ross Boylan wrote:
> Two questions.
>
> 1. If I provide a function that returns a list of lists, do the inner
> lists need to have entries for the transformed parameters (that is,
> items defined in the transformed parameters block)?

No. Only the parameters are read --- everything else is ignored.
The parameters are then used to define the transformed params.

We have an item on the to-do list to allow partial inits, but
so far, you need to specify a value for every parameter.

There's another to-do item to provide a controllable degree of
randomization around an initial value.

Don't know when either of these will make their way to the code.

> I would have
> thought not, but I notice that get_inits() returns inner lists that do
> have those parameters.
>
> 2. Suppose my init function calls random number generators. If I
> provide a seed argument to the stan call is that sufficient to assure
> I'll get the same inits if I rerun with the same seed?

In R, the init function is going to be governed by R's RNG, not
Stan's. I don't know if RStan set's R's RNG seed using the
seed supplied to the stan() call or not.

> I'm also a bit confused by the remark that the init function can take an
> optional chain_id argument. Should such a function return just the
> inner list, or does it need to return a list of lists (with the outer
> list having only one element?).
The function should return a single list of values for all parameters.

> If I use such a function does it change
> the answers for 1 or 2?

Not to 1, but I didn't completely answer 2.

- Bob

On 11/6/2013 10:02 PM, Ross Boylan wrote:
> Two questions.

> 1. If I provide a function that returns a list of lists, do the inner
> lists need to have entries for the transformed parameters (that is,
> items defined in the transformed parameters block)? I would have
> thought not, but I notice that get_inits() returns inner lists that do
> have those parameters.

I did a little test. I used lists rather than functions returning lists.
The answer is no, you do not need to provide transformed parameter
initial values.
If you do provide them, the values are ignored

I provided the "wrong" value for the transformed parameter*. The model
ran without complaint, and the value returned by get_inits() had an
initial value for the transformed parameter that was based on my
untransformed value, rather than the init I passed in. Further, the
simulated parameter values were identical in the 2 runs.

Ross

* Original parameter was alpha_raw with initial value 1.
Transformed parameter was alpha, defined with alpha <- 2*alpha_raw.
Specified initial value of alpha as 0 which is not 2*1.
get_inits returns alpha=2.

On 11/8/13, 6:17 PM, Ross Boylan wrote:
> On 11/6/2013 10:02 PM, Ross Boylan wrote:
>> Two questions.
>>
>> 1. If I provide a function that returns a list of lists, do the inner
>> lists need to have entries for the transformed parameters (that is,
>> items defined in the transformed parameters block)? I would have
>> thought not, but I notice that get_inits() returns inner lists that do
>> have those parameters.

> I did a little test. I used lists rather than functions returning lists.
> The answer is no, you do not need to provide transformed parameter initial values.
> If you do provide them, the values are ignored

Sorry --- I thought I'd answered that already.

This is indeed the intended behavior --- only the parameters
are read. This has to be the behavior because the transformed
parameters are a deterministic function of the parameters, so
there's nothing else to specify.

I made a note to make this clear in the next release of the manual:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/325

- Bob
